title: Restore focus-visible and ARIA semantics for compact chips, sticky table headers, and chart brush controls
creator: Aisha Bennet
description: Address regressions introduced by the compact density token migration that removed visible focus outlines and altered ARIA labeling for chips, table sticky headers, and brush controls in charts. Deliver a set of design and code changes plus VPAT evidence to restore keyboard discoverability and ensure WCAG AA contrast and semantic roles across affected components.
acceptance_criteria: All compact chip variants display a clear focus-visible outline (>= 2px) following the current token contrast ramp when focused via keyboard
Sticky table headers announce their presence to screen readers and maintain correct tab order for header controls (filters/sort buttons)
Chart brush and lasso controls have accessible labels, aria-pressed/aria-checked semantics as appropriate, and keyboard equivalents for starting/committing a brush
Automated Storybook visual snapshots capture focused states for compact tokens across light/dark themes
VPAT artifact updated with end-to-end test cases, manual evidence screenshots, and notes for remediation steps
Design sign-off and engineering PR merged with unit/integration tests and a small regression checklist
notes: Root cause: compact density token change removed focus stroke token and a CSS specificity change in chips overrode :focus-visible rules
Temporary mitigation shipped in runtime-1.18 for customers with strict keyboard-only workflows; this ticket aims for a durable design-system-level fix
Cross-team check with product-management for any interaction changes that may affect downstream plugin behavior (filter chips are consumed by table-scripting)
decisions: Restore a dedicated 'focus-ring-compact' token with higher contrast prioritized over decorative outlines
Use role="toolbar" and aria-label on sticky header containers to improve screen reader context, rather than adding hidden headings that complicate DOM order
For chart brush, implement keyboard binding 'Space' to start/commit and 'Escape' to cancel, expose aria-roledescription 'brush control' and aria-live region updates during operations
tradeoffs: Larger focus rings in compact density consume slightly more visual space — chosen to prioritize accessibility over strict compactness
Implementing keyboard-first brush interactions requires small additions to chart runtime API; increases surface area but improves automation/testability
